quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Change your lane position as needed based on conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight for better visibility.
Follow closely behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position as needed based on conditions.
questions.explanation: Be flexible about where you ride in your lane, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are poor.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes of starting to ride.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Stopping will be easier than without a sidecar.
Stopping will take longer than without a sidecar.
Stopping is about the same as without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer than without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle, which increases the braking force you need. Slowing and stopping take longer with a sidecar, especially on downhill slopes.

questions.question: Which of the following will protect your eyes from the wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When should the front brake be used?

options.text: Any time you slow down or stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you slow down or stop
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you are not going slowly enough when shifting into a lower gear, what could happen?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid. This could cause you to lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: When being passed, all of the following are potential hazards, except:

options.text: Objects being thrown from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors, wind gusts, and objects passengers might throw. Headlights from the passing vehicle are not a hazard.

questions.question: When riding in a group and passing another vehicle, it is best to:

options.text: Have one rider finish passing before the next rider starts.
Have several riders pass at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to show no other motorcycles are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have one rider finish passing before the next rider starts.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, pass one at a time. Each rider should complete their pass and get back in formation before the next rider passes.

questions.question: Compared to daytime riding, a rider at night should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Leave more distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.explanation: At night, slow down and increase your following distance to avoid crashes. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Be flexible about your lane position at night.

questions.question: The body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drinks seven drinks over three hours, how many drinks likely remain in their system three hours after their last drink?
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. For example: seven drinks consumed over three hours leaves about four drinks in the system three hours later.

questions.question: What color are warning signs, and what color is the lettering?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when preparing to pass a vehicle on the left?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center portions of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you the best view of the passing lane.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes of starting to ride.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist tell a passenger to do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Mount the motorcycle after the motorcycle has been started.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mount the motorcycle after the motorcycle has been started.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers to get on after you start the engine. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you. They should hold your waist, hips, or belt firmly and keep both feet on the footrests at all times.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: Can limit the view of the motorcycle operator.
Allow the motorcycle operator to see as far to the sides as necessary.
Do not have to be worn if the motorcycle operator thinks their view would be limited.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle operator to see as far to the sides as necessary.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not limit your vision. They allow you to see far to the sides for safe riding.

questions.question: What best protects your eyes from wind while riding?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This lets experienced riders watch them from the back.

questions.question: Which action will NOT reduce your chances of an accident?
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay alert, identify hazards, use your headlight to be visible, and keep space around your motorcycle. Riding without a headlight makes you harder to see and increases danger.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate or brake during a wobble. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Shift your weight forward and down, then pull off the road as soon as possible.

questions.question: What happens to your steering if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire will make your steering feel heavy. If you notice heavy steering, pull over safely and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Throttle down and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes together. Squeeze them firmly and stay calm even if the brakes lock up.

questions.question: How can you be more visible to other drivers at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as closely as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Riding with your headlight on is the best way to help others see you at an intersection. Keep your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply pressure smoothly and steadily, increasing force as needed.

questions.question: What is the best way to make a quick stop?

options.text: Throttle down and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: When you need to stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes together.
